items.title: Section: Eight Stages of Life, Gradual and Sudden Realisation, the Nine Sequential Absorptions, and the Order of the Three Trainings

items.zh: 或有增長次第，謂嬰孩、童子等八位次第生起。或有現觀次第，謂於苦等四聖諦中次第現觀。或有入定次第，謂次第入九次第定。或有修學次第，謂增上戒學為依，次生增上心學；增上心學為依，後生增上慧學。
items.en:
Fourth, growth sequence. There is growth sequence: infancy, childhood, and the rest of the eight stages arising in succession.
Fifth, sequence of direct realisation. There is sequence of direct realisation: directly realising the four noble truths of suffering and the rest in succession.
Sixth, sequence of meditative absorption. There is sequence of meditative absorption: entering the nine sequential attainments in succession.
Seventh, sequence of spiritual training. There is sequence of spiritual training: relying on the training in heightened ethical discipline, the training in heightened mind then arises; relying on the training in heightened mind, the training in heightened wisdom arises afterwards.

items.title: Section: Time and Number, Both Merely Designated — And All Thirteen Items of This Analysis Now Complete

items.zh: 復次，云何時？謂由日輪出沒增上力故，安立顯示時節差別；又由諸行生滅增上力故，安立顯示世位差別；總說名時。此時差別復有多種。謂時、年、月、半月、晝、夜、剎那、臘縛、牟呼栗多等位，及與過去、未來、現在。復次，云何數？謂安立顯示各別事物計算數量差別，是名為數。此數差別復有多種。謂一數、二數，從此已去皆名多數。又數邊際名阿僧企耶，自此已去，一切算數所不能轉，是故數之邊際名不可數。
items.en:
Twelfth, time; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is time? Second, the explanation; first, clarifying its establishment. Through the rising and setting of the sun, one provisionally designates and reveals the distinctions among seasons and hours; through the arising and ceasing of conditioned phenomena, one provisionally designates and reveals the distinctions among the time-periods — together these are simply called time.
Thirteenth, number; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is number? Second, the explanation; first, clarifying its establishment. The provisional designation revealing the distinct quantity of separate things is called number.
Third, revealing its outermost limit. Furthermore, number's own outermost limit is called an asaṃkhyeya; beyond this, no calculation whatsoever remains possible — therefore number's own limit is called the uncountable.

items.title: Section: What a Seed Is Not — and Why the Very Same Thing Is Called Both Seed and Fruit

items.zh: 復次，種子云何？非析諸行別有實物名為種子，亦非餘處。然即諸行如是種性、如是等生、如是安布，名為種子，亦名為果。
items.en:
Second, extensively explaining seeds; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is a seed?
Second, the explanation; first, revealing its essential nature; first, clarifying what it is not. A seed is not some separate, substantially real thing found by analysing conditioned phenomena, nor is it found elsewhere.
Second, revealing the correct view; first, its other names. This same conditioned phenomenon, considered as such a lineage, as what gives rise to a corresponding manifestation, and as what is thus deposited, is called a seed — and is equally called a fruit.

items.title: Section: Seed and Fruit Never Blur — Illustrated Through a Single Grain of Wheat

items.zh: 當知此中，果與種子不相雜亂。何以故？若望過去諸行，即此名果；若望未來諸行，即此名種子。如是若時望彼名為種子，非於爾時即名為果；若時望彼名果，非於爾時即名種子。是故當知種子與果不相雜亂。譬如穀、麥等物，所有芽、莖、葉等種子，於彼物中磨擣分析，求異種子了不可得，亦非餘處。然諸大種如是種性、如是等生、如是安布，即穀、麥等物能為彼緣，令彼得生，說名種子。當知此中道理亦爾。
items.en:
Second, revealing they are never confused; first, stating it. One should know that, within this teaching, fruit and seed are never confused with one another. Second, the question raised. Why is this so? Third, the explanation; first, distinguished by what is regarded. Considered in relation to past conditioned phenomena, this very phenomenon is called a fruit; considered in relation to future conditioned phenomena, this very phenomenon is called a seed.
Second, distinguished by stage. Whenever regarded as a seed at a given time, it is not, at that same time, called a fruit; whenever regarded as a fruit, it is not, at that same time, called a seed. Fourth, the conclusion. Therefore one should know that seed and fruit are never confused with one another.
Third, citing a simile. Just as with grain, wheat, and the like, the sprout, stalk, and leaf all have their own seed — yet if one grinds, pounds, and analyses that thing, no separate seed can ever be found, nor is it found elsewhere. Yet the great elements, precisely as this kind of nature, as what gives rise to a corresponding manifestation, and as what is deposited within it, constitute the very grain and wheat that serve as the condition for that sprout, stalk, and leaf to arise — this is why they are called its seed. Fourth, the combined conclusion. One should know that the principle here is exactly the same.

items.title: Section: Four Ways a Wholesome Seed Itself Can Be Weakened — From Habitual Vice to the Arhat's Final Relinquishing

items.zh: 問：前已說損伏染法種子，善法種子損伏云何？答：若常殷重習善相違諸染污法，是初損伏。若執取邪見、多習邪見如諸外道，是第二損伏。若多修習邪見誹謗，如斷善根者，是第三損伏。若能永害染法種子，如前已說，是第四損伏。
items.en:
Second, distinguishing suppression; first, the question posed. Question: having already explained the suppression of defiled phenomena's seeds, how are wholesome seeds themselves suppressed?
Second, the answer; first, the initial suppression. Answer: constantly and earnestly cultivating defiled states directly opposed to wholesome qualities is the first suppression.
Second, the second suppression. Clinging to wrong views and repeatedly cultivating them, as non-Buddhist practitioners do, is the second suppression.
Third, the third suppression. Repeatedly cultivating wrong views to the point of denunciation, as in one who severs their own wholesome roots, is the third suppression.
Fourth, the fourth suppression. Being capable of permanently destroying defiled phenomena's seeds, as already explained before, is the fourth suppression.

items.title: Section: Nine Kinds of Seed — Already Ripened or Not, Weak or Fully Matured, Suppressed or Free

items.zh: 復次，若略說一切種子，當知有九種。一、已與果，二、未與果，三、果正現前，四、果不現前，五、軟品，六、中品，七、上品，八、被損伏，九、不被損伏。若已與果，此名果正現前；若果正現前，此名已與果。若未與果，此名果不現前；若果不現前，此名未與果。若住本性，名軟品；若修、若練善不善法未到究竟，名中品；若修、若練已到究竟，名上品。損及不損，如前應知。
items.en:
Third, distinguishing its kinds; first, stating and listing. Furthermore, in brief, all seeds should be known to be of nine kinds: first, already having yielded a result; second, not yet having yielded a result; third, its result currently manifesting; fourth, its result not currently manifesting; fifth, the weak grade; sixth, the middling grade; seventh, the superior grade; eighth, being suppressed; ninth, not being suppressed.
Second, explaining each; first, already/not-yet yielding a result. Whenever a seed has already yielded its result, this is called its result currently manifesting; whenever its result is currently manifesting, this is called already having yielded a result. Whenever a seed has not yet yielded its result, this is called its result not currently manifesting; whenever its result is not currently manifesting, this is called not yet having yielded a result.
Second, the weak, middling, and superior grades. Remaining in its original condition is called the weak grade; being cultivated towards wholesome or unwholesome conduct without yet reaching completion is called the middling grade; being cultivated to the point of completion is called the superior grade.
Third, being suppressed and not being suppressed. Being suppressed and not being suppressed should be understood exactly as explained before.

items.title: Section: What a Seed Ultimately Is — Neither Simply Real Nor Simply Unreal, Exactly Like Suchness Itself

items.zh: 復次，我當略說安立種子。云何略說安立種子？謂於阿賴耶識中，一切諸法遍計自性妄執習氣，是名安立種子。然此習氣是實物有、是世俗有。望彼諸法，不可定說異不異相，猶如真如。即此亦名遍行麁重。
items.en:
Fourth, clarifying seed's establishment; first, stating this. Furthermore, I shall now briefly explain how seed is established. Second, raising the question. How, in brief, is seed established?
Third, explaining the meaning; first, briefly distinguishing its character; first, revealing its essential nature. Within the store-consciousness, the habitual residue of every phenomenon's imagined, clung-to self-nature is called an established seed.
Second, distinguishing whether it is provisional or real. This habitual residue is substantially existent, yet also conventionally existent.
Third, clarifying whether it is different or the same. In relation to those phenomena, one cannot definitively say its characteristic is different or not different — exactly like suchness.
Fourth, revealing its further name. This is also called the pervasive coarse burden.

items.title: Section: Where the Seeds of Liberation Actually Come From — Three Historic Positions on Innate and Newly Cultivated Purity

items.zh: 問：若此習氣攝一切種子，復名遍行麁重者，諸出世間法從何種子生？若言麁重自性種子為種子生，不應道理。答：諸出世間法從真如所緣緣種子生，非彼習氣積集種子所生。
items.en:
Second, resolving objections; first, the objection regarding the pervasive coarse burden; first, the question. Question: if this habitual residue encompasses all seeds, and is also called the pervasive coarse burden, from what seed do transmundane phenomena arise? To say they arise from the very seed constituting this coarse burden's own nature would be unreasonable.
Second, the answer. Answer: transmundane phenomena arise from the seed conditioned by taking suchness as an object, not from the seed accumulated through habitual residue.

items.zh: 問：若非習氣積集種子所生者，何因緣故，建立三種般涅槃法種性差別補特伽羅，及建立不般涅槃法種性補特伽羅？所以者何？一切皆

items.title: Section: Why Some Beings Are Śrāvakas, Some Pratyekabuddhas, and Some Buddhas — All Explained Through Obstruction, Which Reveals the Presence or Absence of Uncontaminated Seeds

items.zh: 有真如所緣緣故。答：由有障、無障差別故。若於通達真如所緣緣中有畢竟障種子者，建立為不般涅槃法種性補特伽羅。若不爾者，建立為般涅槃法種性補特伽羅。若有畢竟所知障種子布在所依，非煩惱障種子者，於彼一分建立聲聞種性補特伽羅，一分建立獨覺種性補特伽羅。若不爾者，建立如來種性補特伽羅。是故無過。
items.en:
Second, distinguished by the presence or absence of a cognitive-obstruction seed; first, its presence. Whoever has, deposited within their own basis, a seed of the cognitive obstruction destined never to be removed, without a corresponding seed of the afflictive obstruction destined never to be removed, is established, in one portion, as belonging to the śrāvaka lineage, and in another portion, as belonging to the independently-awakened lineage.
Second, its absence. Whoever is not so, is established as belonging to the tathāgata lineage.
Third, concluding this is correct. Therefore there is no fault in this account.

items.title: Section: When the Transmundane Path Arises, the Store-Consciousness Itself Is Overturned — And Fascicle 52 Closes on Seed's Final Lesson

items.zh: 若出世間諸法生已，即便隨轉，當知由轉依力所任持故。然此轉依與阿賴耶識互相違反，對治阿賴耶識，名無漏界，離諸戲論。
items.en:
Second, revealing what continues after; first, presenting the transformed basis. Once transmundane phenomena have arisen, they immediately continue on — one should know this is sustained by the power of the transformed basis.
Second, explaining its character. This transformed basis stands in mutual opposition to the store-consciousness, counteracting it — it is called the uncontaminated realm, free of all conceptual proliferation.
Studying the true nature of seeds should offer the Buddha's disciples a genuinely sobering lesson: whatever has been done definitely leaves behind a trace — so every person must be careful in thought, speech, and action. Every arising thought and every deed of body, speech, and mind becomes a kind of disposition, a functional capacity, a seed, stored within the store-consciousness, ready to manifest again whenever the right conditions converge — this too should remind the Buddha's disciples to diligently cultivate ethical discipline, concentration, and wisdom, so as to extinguish greed, hatred, and delusion.

blocks.text: The fascicle ends with the central idea of Yogācāra: seeds. What are they, where do the seeds of liberation come from, and what happens to the store-consciousness at liberation?
Master Cháng Bǎi: discipline is the foundation, concentration the aid, and wisdom what cuts afflictions at the root.

The sun's rising and setting reveals the hours; the arising and ceasing of things reveals the three times. Master Cháng Bǎi: in suffering, time passes slowly; in joy, quickly. Time too is a designation.
"Not a separate real thing found by analysing phenomena, nor found elsewhere." Master Cháng Bǎi: a seed is a capacity, not a thing with substance; seeds and phenomena are not separate.

Constant evil, clinging to wrong views, rejecting the good (as in severing wholesome roots), and destroying defiled seeds. Master Cháng Bǎi: when an arhat enters nirvāṇa without remainder, even good and neutral seeds are left behind; yet if a buddha urges them, they will turn towards awakening.
Remaining in its original state, a seed is weak; cultivated incompletely, middling; cultivated fully, superior.
Master Cháng Bǎi: relative to the imagined nature, a seed is real; relative to the perfected nature, it is conventional.

Transmundane things arise "from the seed conditioned by taking suchness as an object". Master Cháng Bǎi reports several views: some say these seeds are innate; others that innate seeds without new cultivation cannot produce the noble path.

(Untranslated, 0589a17: the question why there are beings of three lineages, and some without lineage for nirvāṇa.) The two vehicles' lineages are set up by a seed of cognitive obstruction that can never be removed.

The transformed basis stands opposed to the store-consciousness and is "the uncontaminated realm, free of all conceptual proliferation". Master Cháng Bǎi: only the name of the store-consciousness tied to defilement is severed.
Four conditions, the "dissociated formations", and seeds. Its lesson is that most of what we treat as solid things (time, number, life, even "attainment") are names laid on a flow of causes.

quiz.q: What is the sequence of spiritual training?
options: relying on heightened ethical discipline, heightened mind arises; relying on heightened mind, heightened wisdom arises
relying on heightened wisdom, heightened mind then arises; relying on heightened mind, heightened ethical discipline arises afterwards
relying on heightened mind, heightened discipline arises; relying on that, heightened wisdom arises
the three are trained at once, with no order of reliance
quiz.why: The treatise states the order of reliance: discipline, then mind, then wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: discipline is the foundation, concentration the aid, and wisdom is what can cut off afflictions at the root.

quiz.q: How does the treatise establish time?
options: by the sun's rising and setting for seasons and hours, by the arising and ceasing of phenomena for the time-periods
by the arising and ceasing of phenomena for seasons and hours, by the sun's rising and setting for the time-periods
time is real and exists apart from phenomena
by the moon's phases for seasons, by karma for the time-periods
quiz.why: The treatise says the sun's rising and setting reveals seasons and hours, the arising and ceasing of phenomena reveals the time-periods, and together these are called time. Master Cháng Bǎi: days are established from the sun coming out and going down.

quiz.q: What is the outermost limit of number called?
options: an asaṃkhyeya; beyond it no calculation is possible, hence the uncountable
the sands of the Ganges, because no one can count them
a great eon, because it is the longest time
eighty thousand, because it is the extreme measure of lifespan and eons
quiz.why: The treatise says number's limit is called an asaṃkhyeya; beyond this no calculation remains possible, and so the limit is called the uncountable. Master Cháng Bǎi: from the asaṃkhyeya onward, no calculation can go further.

quiz.q: Why does Master Cháng Bǎi say time, too, is provisional?
options: it feels slow in suffering and fast in joy, varying with the mind
clocks differ from place to place, with no one standard at all
there is really no rising or setting of the sun
time and space are one and the same substance
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in times of suffering one feels time passes slowly, and when glad and happy one feels it passes quickly, so time too is a provisionally established phenomenon.

quiz.q: Is a seed a separate real thing found by analysing conditioned phenomena?
options: yes: analysis of phenomena reveals a separate real thing
no, but it can be found elsewhere, apart from phenomena
yes: a seed is a form made of ultimate particles
no: it is neither a separate real thing found by analysis, nor found elsewhere
quiz.why: The treatise says a seed is not a separate real thing found by analysing phenomena, nor found elsewhere. Master Cháng Bǎi: nor can a seed be found apart from all conditioned phenomena; that is to say, phenomena and seeds are not separate.

quiz.q: The English adds "spiritual disposition" and "deposited within the store-consciousness." How does this fare in the grain simile?
options: the Chinese does name the store-consciousness here, and the English renders it faithfully, so it reads smoothly in the grain simile and needs no change at all
grain has nothing spiritual and the text here names no store-consciousness; the lecture calls a seed a capacity, not a real thing
grain has consciousness, so "spiritual" fits well
種性 means buddha-nature, so "spiritual disposition" is right
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a seed is a capacity, not a thing with real substance, found neither in conditioned phenomena nor apart from them. The Chinese here speaks of the great elements of grain and wheat. "Spiritual disposition" and "deposited within the store-consciousness" are additions that do not fit the simile, and the latter is not in the Chinese.

quiz.q: What is the first suppression of wholesome seeds?
options: constantly and earnestly cultivating defiled states opposed to the wholesome
clinging to wrong views and repeatedly cultivating them, as outsiders do, so good does not arise
cultivating wrong views to the point of denunciation
permanently destroying the seeds of defilement
quiz.why: The treatise lists four suppressions in order: constant cultivation of defilement opposed to the good, clinging to wrong views, denunciation as in severing wholesome roots, and destroying defiled seeds. Master Cháng Bǎi on the first: constantly doing evil is itself suppression of the good.

quiz.q: Why is permanently destroying defiled seeds nevertheless counted as a fourth suppression of wholesome seeds, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: entering nirvāṇa without remainder, an arhat abandons good and neutral seeds too; yet urged by a buddha, one may still turn to the Great Vehicle
destroying defiled seeds turns good seeds into evil ones
with defiled seeds gone, good seeds lose their opposite and flourish
this is an error in the text; there are really only three
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when an arhat's life ends and they enter nirvāṇa without remainder, even the good and neutral seeds within are all abandoned. Yet he adds that when conditions meet and a buddha urges them to give rise to the mind of awakening, they will turn from the Lesser to the Great Vehicle.

quiz.q: How are the weak, middling, and superior grades of seeds distinguished?
options: remaining in its original condition is weak; cultivated without reaching completion is middling; cultivated to completion is superior
not yet yielding a result is weak; its result currently manifesting is middling; already having yielded a result is superior, graded by whether the result manifests
unwholesome is weak; neutral is middling; wholesome is superior
suppressed is weak; unsuppressed is middling; destroyed is superior
quiz.why: The treatise grades seeds by cultivation: remaining in its original condition is weak, cultivated without completion is middling, and cultivated to completion is superior. Note that it speaks of wholesome and unwholesome alike. Master Cháng Bǎi: a seed's capacity keeping its original state is the weak grade.

quiz.q: The treatise calls habitual residue both "substantially existent" and "conventionally existent." How does Master Cháng Bǎi reconcile these?
options: it is substantially existent relative to the perfected, and conventionally existent relative to the imagined, the two running in those directions
defiled seeds are real and pure seeds conventional
real while manifesting, conventional while not
it is substantially existent relative to the imagined, and conventionally existent relative to the perfected
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: relative to the imagined nature it is substantially existent, and relative to the perfected nature it is conventionally existent. The Sub-commentary likewise places it under the dependent nature, real in that sense, and conventional because of its defiled nature.

quiz.q: From what seed do transmundane phenomena arise, according to the treatise?
options: the seed constituting the coarse burden's own nature, that is, of the pervasive coarse burden itself, accumulated through this residue
the seed conditioned by taking suchness as an object, not the seed accumulated through habitual residue
the seed accumulated through habitual residue
no seed at all, arising by a noble one's blessing
quiz.why: The treatise rejects the seed of the coarse burden's own nature and answers that transmundane phenomena arise from the seed conditioned by taking suchness as an object. Master Cháng Bǎi: they must arise from a seed having suchness as object condition, not from a seed accumulated by affliction and habit.

quiz.q: On the source of undefiled seeds, what does Master Cháng Bǎi report?
options: a single view: all undefiled seeds come only from new habituation
one view: those with the lineage have innate undefiled seeds as causal condition; yet without new habituation to strengthen them, the noble path does not arise
a single view: innate seeds produce the path of themselves, with no habituation
all say the undefiled has no seed and arises directly from suchness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi reports several views. One says beings with the lineage realise suchness with innate undefiled seeds as causal condition; another notes that though seeds are innate, without new habituation to strengthen them they cannot produce the noble path. The English treats "the seed conditioned by taking suchness" as settled, while the lecture lists differing readings.

quiz.q: The English says "destined never to be removed" for 畢竟. What is the function of 畢竟 in this definition of the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha lineages?
options: the two vehicles have a cognitive-obstruction seed never to be removed, and no afflictive one never to be removed; the English brings out 畢竟
the two vehicles have no afflictive seeds at all from birth
both obstructions of the two vehicles are never to be removed
their cognitive-obstruction seed is removed only at buddhahood, so 畢竟 here means "finally, in the end," which the English has reversed
quiz.why: The treatise establishes the two lineages by a seed of cognitive obstruction never to be removed, without a like seed of afflictive obstruction. The two vehicles still have afflictive seeds that can be severed; what they lack is one never to be removed. The English "destined never to be removed" keeps this, while the lecture's paraphrase omits the word. Master Cháng Bǎi: the lineages are set by presence or absence of obstruction.

quiz.q: How does the transformed basis relate to the store-consciousness?
options: they are identical, with only a difference of name
the transformed basis gives rise to the store-consciousness as its support
they stand in mutual opposition; it counteracts the store-consciousness, is called the uncontaminated realm, and is free of proliferation
they accord with each other and jointly sustain the transmundane
quiz.why: The treatise says the transformed basis stands in mutual opposition to the store-consciousness, counteracting it, and is called the uncontaminated realm, free of all conceptual proliferation. Master Cháng Bǎi: the transformed basis is pure and the store-consciousness defiled.

quiz.q: If the transformed basis counteracts the store-consciousness, what is actually severed, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the very substance of the eighth consciousness, so that no mind remains and only suchness is left, which is called the transformed basis
the undefiled seeds, leaving only pure suchness
only the name of the store-consciousness tied to defilement; through practice, what one relied on becomes uncontaminated
the first six consciousnesses, the eighth remaining unchanged
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: only the name of the store-consciousness tied to defiled phenomena is severed. Ordinary beings originally relied on the store-consciousness, and now through practice it is turned into the uncontaminated, which is called transformation of basis.
